title: Introduce background arena compaction and synchronized device frees to mitigate cross-deployment GPU OOMs
creator: Aarti Mehta
description: Several customers (hosted, Dedicated pools and two Private on-prem clusters) reported intermittent GPU OOMs during normal inference workloads. Investigation shows a combination of device allocator arena fragmentation, delayed/async device frees for pinned buffers, and a concurrent KV cache compaction race that allowed stale pointers into reclaimed device memory. This ticket tracks the runtime patch to add background arena compaction, ensure device-side frees are synchronized where necessary, harden KV compaction with atomic snapshots and CRC checks, and deploy an emergency rollout with a non-disruptive mitigation for running clusters.
acceptance_criteria: No reproducible OOMs in the canonical stress test (batching + variable seq_len) after patch across hosted and Dedicated canaries for 72h
KV cache compaction no longer causes invalid device pointer dereferences under concurrent serve + compaction load in unit + integration tests
Patch released as runtime-1.26.3 with rollout docs and migration instructions for Private customers
Telemetry shows reduction in long-tail per-node GPU memory usage and <1% increase in median latency at target batch sizes
Customer-facing postmortem published and affected customers notified with remediation steps
steps_to_reproduce: Run synthetic workload: 200 concurrent sessions, randomized sequence lengths up to 8192, batching policy 'auto' that results in wide batch-size variance
Enable KV cache with compaction interval = 5s and 128MB shard size to stress concurrent compaction
Observe intermittent CUDA OOMs after 30-90 minutes correlating with compaction windows and peak batched allocations
Reproduce locally with stress harness: nohup ./stress_test --batch-variance --kvcache-compaction=5s > out.log &
mitigation_and_workarounds: Immediate: reduce max_batch_size and set kvcache.compaction_interval=30s for affected Dedicated pools and Hosted beta regions
Hotfix: restart runtime process on nodes hitting OOMs to force full device memory reclamation (documented as emergency step for Private customers)
Rolling: apply conservative backpressure (throttle large batch assembly) in the router in front of canary nodes
Long-term: deploy runtime-1.26.3 which includes compact_arena + synchronized frees + KV compaction hardening
implementation_notes: Add GPUAllocator::compact_arena(threshold_bytes, max_passes) that coalesces free chunks and returns a compaction report
Introduce DeviceFreeFence that forces a cudaDeviceSynchronize() for frees of pinned staging buffers above configurable size; default threshold 8MB
KV cache compaction: take atomic snapshot of shard index, copy live keys to new table, compute per-shard CRC32 and swap via compare-and-swap; fall back to abort compaction if CRC mismatch
Add refcount and stale-pointer assertions around device-backed KV values to prevent use-after-free in debug builds
Expose compaction metrics: arena_free_ratio, compact_passes, compaction_failures, kvcache_compaction_latency
Avoid blocking application threads in hot path: background compactor runs on dedicated runtime worker and yields to latency-critical pathways when per-token latency crosses SLO threshold
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary hosted): deploy to 2 nodes in us-west-2 Hosted pool with full telemetry collection; run 72h soak
Stage 2 (Dedicated canaries): deploy to 3 Dedicated nodes across two customers who volunteered for canary; maintain reduced batch sizes for 24h while verifying memory trends
Stage 3 (Private): ship patch and migration script to on-prem customers with pre-check script to collect allocator stats; offer remote support window for automated application restart if needed
Rollback: revert to previous runtime and re-enable emergency throttling if compaction causes regressions
Communication: notify affected customers before and after each stage; include mitigation steps and expected maintenance windows
testing_plan: Unit tests for GPUAllocator compaction logic and DeviceFreeFence behavior
Integration test: end-to-end PKB stress harness replicating customer workload for 72h (hosted + dedicated config)
Fuzzer: random concurrent compaction + serve operations for KV cache for 1M iterations
Performance: measure p50/p95/p99 latency and token/sec before/after to ensure <5% median latency regression
Safety: run debug build on small cluster to validate refcount assertions and zone checks
Private customer verification: provide a lightweight test harness and run with each private customer for acceptance
